features.evidence: Bachelor's degree / Master's degree / Doctoral degree
features.name: Academic attainment
features.description: Captures the formal level of computer science education the applicant presents relative to the posting's minimum and preferred qualifications.

levels.descriptor: No relevant degree is stated, or the educational background is unclear or outside the field.
The letter states a bachelor's degree or equivalent relevant preparation.
The letter states a master's degree in computer science or a related technical field.
The letter states a doctoral degree in computer science or a related technical field.

features.evidence: 3 years / 5 years / 7 years of software development
features.name: Relevant tenure
features.description: Captures how much directly relevant software engineering experience the letter claims.

levels.descriptor: Relevant software engineering experience is below the minimum or not clearly stated.
The letter shows roughly minimum-level tenure, such as about 2 to 3 years.
The letter shows solid mid-level tenure, such as about 4 to 5 years.
The letter shows extensive tenure for this role, such as 6 or more years.

features.name: Production service breadth
features.description: Captures the volume of real production systems the applicant says they have tested, maintained, or launched.

levels.descriptor: Little production breadth is evidenced, or shipped systems are not clearly described.
The letter points to work on 1 to 2 production services.
The letter points to work on 3 to 4 production services.
The letter points to work on 5 or more production services.

features.evidence: Python became my workhorse for everything operational
features.name: Python depth
features.description: Captures how substantively the letter shows production Python experience beyond a passing mention.

levels.descriptor: Python is absent or appears only incidentally.
Python is mentioned as a tool or companion language, but depth is unclear.
The letter shows regular production Python use for tooling, automation, prototypes, or services.
Python is portrayed as a major production language with broad, concrete use across services, automation, and agent behavior.

features.evidence: redesigning an in-memory index on our hottest request path
features.name: Algorithmic rigor
features.description: Captures whether the applicant demonstrates practical fluency with data structures and algorithms through concrete system improvements.

levels.descriptor: No meaningful evidence of data structures or algorithms ability is given.
The letter claims algorithmic strength, but evidence is generic or thin.
The letter gives a concrete example of using better structures or algorithms to improve a system.
The letter shows strong practical algorithmic judgment on a complex or performance-critical system.

features.evidence: shipped LLM-backed features with the evaluation needed to trust them
features.name: Applied AI maturity
features.description: Captures the depth of production experience with AI systems, especially whether the letter addresses reliability, evaluation, or guardrails.

levels.descriptor: No relevant AI experience is mentioned.
AI is mentioned, but the work sounds exploratory or underspecified.
The letter shows shipped AI or LLM functionality in production.
The letter shows production AI work plus attention to evaluation, reliability, hardening, or guardrails.

features.evidence: performed security assessments, from threat models to code review
features.name: Security assessment depth
features.description: Captures how directly the letter shows hands-on ability to assess systems for security risk.

levels.descriptor: No hands-on security assessment work is shown.
The letter gestures at security review, but methods or responsibility are unclear.
The letter names concrete assessment work such as threat modeling, code review, attack-surface review, or service reviews.
The letter shows substantial assessment ownership, including attacker-oriented analysis, formal review work, or validation of fixes and remediation.

features.evidence: automated the intake and triage of vulnerability reports
features.name: Vulnerability handling automation
features.description: Captures whether the applicant has built systems that reduce manual work in vulnerability report intake, classification, routing, or follow-through.

levels.descriptor: No experience with vulnerability intake or response automation is shown.
The letter mentions vulnerability work, but not a clear automated system.
The letter clearly describes automation for vulnerability triage, routing, classification, or queue handling.
The letter describes an end-to-end vulnerability-handling pipeline with details such as deduplication, prioritization, variant analysis, or explicit reduction of manual workload.

features.evidence: Python agents plan and act while Go services provide the guardrails
features.name: Agentic systems design
features.description: Captures experience designing agent-based tooling, especially controlled architectures that pair autonomous components with explicit constraints.

levels.descriptor: No agent-based tooling experience is shown.
The letter mentions agents or autonomous workflows only in general terms.
The letter describes a recognizable agent architecture, typically pairing Python agents with Go services.
The letter shows deliberate control design for agents, such as permissions, auditability, bounded actions, or explicit end-to-end ownership.

features.name: Security automation motivation
features.description: Captures how clearly the letter frames the role as a mission to scale security through engineering rather than as a generic software job.

levels.descriptor: Interest in the role is generic and could fit many software jobs.
The letter shows some interest in security or backend impact, but the motivation stays broad.
The letter clearly wants to make secure behavior easier by default or reduce repetitive security toil.
The letter offers a nuanced philosophy of security automation as leverage, capacity creation, or quiet resilience.

features.evidence: improvements there are inherited by every team downstream
features.name: Platform leverage orientation
features.description: Captures whether the applicant explicitly values foundational systems because they create organization-wide leverage.

levels.descriptor: The letter does not emphasize organization-wide leverage or foundational work.
The letter mentions scale in general terms.
The letter clearly prefers foundational or platform work because benefits spread across many teams.
The letter repeatedly frames impact in multiplier-effect terms and ties that framing to how the applicant chooses work.

features.evidence: the best tooling I have ever built came directly from that kind of proximity
features.name: Internal customer empathy
features.description: Captures whether the applicant emphasizes serving developer teams by reducing friction and building around real user needs.

levels.descriptor: The letter does not show much attention to the developer teams who would use the tools.
The letter shows a general collaborative tone but little user-centered detail.
The letter explicitly emphasizes reducing friction for engineers or helping teams do the secure thing easily.
The letter gives a concrete, user-centered view of tooling, such as learning from proximity to users or designing around real team pain.

features.evidence: replicated cache with proper failover from scratch
features.name: Concreteness of evidence
features.description: Captures how much the letter relies on specific, role-relevant examples instead of unsubstantiated claims.

levels.descriptor: The letter relies mostly on assertions, adjectives, or resume-like claims.
The letter includes a few examples, but many claims remain abstract.
The letter supports major claims with several concrete systems, projects, or scenarios.
The letter is dense with specific, role-relevant evidence across multiple claims rather than depending on general statements.

features.evidence: the team now barely thinks about it
features.name: Impact articulation
features.description: Captures whether the letter explains what changed because of the applicant's work rather than only what they built.

levels.descriptor: The letter says what was built but not what changed because of it.
Useful outcomes are implied, but benefits remain mostly unstated.
The letter names clear operational effects such as bottlenecks removed, queues tamed, or manual work reduced.
The letter explicitly connects work to leverage outcomes such as expert hours returned, self-serve operation, or broader protective coverage.

features.name: Security credential strength
features.description: Captures the level of formal external validation of the applicant's security knowledge or hands-on security skill.

levels.descriptor: No external security credential is mentioned.
The letter cites a baseline credential that signals fundamentals, such as Security+.
The letter cites a hands-on credential that signals practical offensive skill, such as OSCP.

features.name: Offensive security practice
features.description: Captures whether the applicant shows ongoing attacker-oriented practice outside routine product work.

levels.descriptor: No ongoing attacker-oriented practice is mentioned.
The letter mentions occasional or light offensive practice, such as infrequent CTF play.
The letter shows regular, intentional offensive practice through recurring CTF participation or similar work.
The letter shows sustained offensive practice with notable results or a clearly articulated learning discipline.

features.evidence: submit corrective patches upstream / maintain a public open-source project
features.name: Open-source ownership
features.description: Captures the depth of the applicant's contribution to external codebases, from opportunistic fixes to sustained maintainership.

levels.descriptor: No open-source contribution is mentioned.
The letter mentions occasional upstream fixes or patches.
The letter shows regular upstream contribution or repeated patching of dependencies.
The letter shows maintainership responsibility, such as owning reviews, releases, or a user community.

features.evidence: distributed task queue with exactly-once semantics
features.name: Personal project ambition
features.description: Captures how much independent technical initiative the letter shows through side projects, especially projects with hard systems or reliability problems.

levels.descriptor: No independent project work is mentioned.
The letter mentions a small utility, app, or lightweight side project.
The letter shows a substantial independent technical build beyond everyday work.
The letter shows an ambitious system built to tackle hard reliability, distribution, recovery, or failure-mode problems.
